items.title: Antigravity CLI 1.5.14 adds live thinking stream, swarm overview, and remote plan mode
facts: Added /thinking to stream the model's full thinking live in the transcript while it thinks and keep finished thoughts expanded without pressing Ctrl+O.

Added a live Overview section to /swarm board on terminals at least 28 rows tall, showing the swarm's goal, overall task progress (Overview · N of M tasks done and any blocked count), and up to six workstream threads with status indicators.
Added plan mode to --remote-agent sessions, so a remote agent can research and write a plan for your review before editing files or running commands.

x_posts.author: @Khaled865412521
x_posts.text:
Antigravity CLI 1.5.14 lets you watch the agent think live. 4 things worth setting today

1. /thinking on
   Off by default. Finished thoughts stay expanded, no Ctrl+O
2. Remote agent can plan first: Shift+Tab into plan, or start with --mode plan
3. /swarm board adds a live Overview: N of M tasks done (terminals 28+ rows tall)
4. Auto mode now reads files outside the workspace without asking. Writes still need approval

agy update

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.330 adds easel chart mod, Enterprise Admin Console sign-in, and worktree safety fixes
facts: Added sign-in to organizations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console: after claude auth login, Claude Code applies the organization's settings and uses its cloud provider or gateway.
Added easel, a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results, on Pro, Max and, where available, Team and Enterprise on macOS and Linux; turn automatic charts off in /config.
Fixed ExitWorktree and the worktree exit dialog deleting a worktree that another running Claude Code session was working in.

x_posts.author: @MegaEvolvedFrog
x_posts.text:
Most of Claude Code v2.1.330 is bug fixes, and the list says a lot about how people run it now

Look at what got fixed:
- settings lost when several processes saved at once
- plugins missing when several plugin commands ran together
- task metadata lost on parallel updates
- a worktree deleted while another session was using it

Same root cause: people run many sessions at the same time

If i were you, i'd stop treating parallel agents as an edge case... update, then check your worktree and settings habits

The tooling is finally catching up with how it's used

How many Claude Code sessions do you run in parallel before things start breaking?

Full article here: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.330

items.title: MomongaCode v0.1.0 launches as open-source terminal coding agent with evidence-backed memory and token efficiency
facts: MomongaCode is a coding agent for the terminal. It works with local and hosted models, keeps its own memory of your repositories, and runs tool calls under a permission system and an operating-system sandbox.
Evidence-backed repo memory: memory and context are built by the runtime from recorded events, not left to the model alone.
Token efficiency ON by default, and a built-in eval command that measures each saving against a baseline with it off.

x_posts.author: @Pro_Algorithm
x_posts.text:
A brand-new FREE coding agent just landed in the terminal... and it's going straight after the two things that make AI coding agents painful: forgetting context and burning tokens.

It's called MomongaCode. v0.1.0 just shipped, open-source and MIT licensed.

What the developer says it packs:
- Works with local AND hosted models
- Evidence-backed repo memory: memory and context are built by the runtime from recorded events, not left to the model alone
- Token efficiency ON by default, and a built-in eval command that measures each saving against a baseline with it off
- OS sandbox, permission rules and "verifiable completion"
- MCP, skills, hooks, background jobs and headless mode

macOS, Linux and Windows. The command is literally "momonga".

Local models + a sandbox + a free license = the kind of agent setup people have been begging for.

It's v0.1, so it's early days. But this is one to watch.

Repo: http://github.com/yuuichieguchi/MomongaCode

 https://x.com/yuuichieguchi/status/2124004883082957280/video/1

items.title: Developers share Claude Code workflows combining Matt Pocock skills with Beads task graphs for parallel agent work
facts: Beads gives your agents a task graph they always remember, even across new sessions.

bd ready shows only the tasks with nothing blocking them; it claims one with bd update --claim, builds it with /implement, which writes tests first and finishes with a code review, then closes it with bd close.
Claims are atomic, so two agents never grab the same task.

items.title: Users report mixed experiences with Antigravity reliability and Neon model performance compared to Claude Code and Codex
facts: Pros: a much better conversation experience than other models rn; surprisingly an entropic beast, able to diversify approaches; code quality is OOM better.
Cons: speed? Neon takes 3-4x longer for response; swarm mode will get stuck waiting for prev step completion.
When I use Codex, OpenCode, or Cursor, the overall workflow generally feels more efficient and predictable.

x_posts.author: @rohanxparmar
x_posts.text:
Insanely cool experience, working on simulating material discovery and verification.

Been running on Antigravity IDE, swarm mode.

Pros:

- a much better conversation experience than other models rn
- surprisingly an entropic beast, able to diversify approaches. Amazing breadth!
- code quality is OOM better

Cons:

- speed? Haven't measured toks/s yet but typically I run the same prompt on multiple models and compare responses. Neon takes 3-4x longer for response.
- less model and more harness, swarm mode will get stuck waiting for prev step completjon. Probably because prev agent doesn't update message board the way it's supposed to on long horizon tasks?

Super close to switching over fully as my daily driver

x_posts.author: @jal_eelll
x_posts.text:
I've been a day one user of antigravity. I used it just last night. Also let's crafiy something. I said Antigravity wasn't freat. I never said it was bad. 

For me, it's mainly the agent execution and overall reliability. Unnecessary tool calls, inconsistent subagent behavior, excessive overhead on simple tasks, and context management (for a while some of my chats would just disappear after an update for example) are areas where I still think Antigravity could improve.

When I use Codex, OpenCode, or Cursor, the overall workflow generally feels more efficient and predictable. I'm not saying Antigravity lacks good features. I love Remote Control, for example. It's just that I have a better experience using these other tools. In my opinion, it even felt better using Gemini models in Cursor than Antigravity. I love Gemini models so I'll always give them and Antigravity a chance but even now I still don't think its neck and neck with the alternatives

items.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform integrates with terminal coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex for MR workflows
facts: Use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or other coding agents with GitLab, so every MR gets the same review, CI fixes, security checks, and approvals.
You can now set up code review, pipeline repair, and security triage together from your coding session.
The GitLab Duo setup skill connects your agent to GitLab and configures automatic review and failed-pipeline repair.

x_posts.author: @theagenticdaily
x_posts.text: GitLab now lets developers trigger its Duo Agent Platform directly from the terminal tools they already use — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Duo CLI. One skill wires these up so agents can turn an issue into a merge request, run automated code review, fix failing pipelines, and triage security findings, all without leaving the terminal. https://about.gitlab.com/blog/agentic-engineering-walkthrough/
